preview: A detailed account of the Barclays Summer Internship selection process, featuring an MCQ and coding round followed by a combined Technical and HR interview.
content: Barclays Interview Experience Hola Amigos! I’m delighted to share that I have been selected by Barclays India for the Summer Internship - BA3 Technology Analyst Internship (Oops! Not a LinkedIn post 😅😂). After a lot of rejections, anxiety, self-doubt, and lack of sleep I am finally here. Following is my overall experience of the selection procedure: Only the CS & IT students from the 3rd year were invited. The basic selection criteria to be eligible to apply for the internship was to have a ≥60% score across class X, XII, and engineering semesters. Round 1: MCQ + Coding questions The eligible students who applied were required to go through the technical test to be shortlisted. The time limit was 1 hour 30 minutes. The breakdown of the test questions was something like this: a. 30 MCQ questions b. 2 Coding questions The MCQ questions were distributed as below. Topics No. of Questions DBMS Around 10 C++ 5 to 7 JavaScript 2 to 3 Python 2 to 3 Java 4 to 5 MongoDB 2 The language-specific questions were about predicting the output of the piece of code given. They framed them such that the basic concepts like functional programming, logical thinking, logical thinking, databases concepts, SQL queries, and OOPs would be covered. Coding Questions: 1. Maximum height of the Factor tree for a given number https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/height-of-factor-tree-for-a-given-number/ 2. Given a graph G with N nodes and an array B of size N such that, element in B represents a directed edge from node i to B[i]. Each node has exactly one outgoing edge from it. Find a path such that max nodes can be covered from the starting point. Print the index of the starting node. If there is more than one solution, print the smallest index. I solved the first question completely using Recursion in C++ with simple division, something like this: int solve(int N, int M) { if ( N == 1 || M == 1 ) return 0; if ( N % M == 0 ) return 1 + solve(M, M - 1); else return solve(N, N - 1); } // Calling the function: int N = 8; cout << solve(N, N - 1); // Output: 2 // O(n) = N For the second question, I ran out of time. The next day morning, I got the mail of getting shortlisted. The interviews were scheduled soon after that! Only 18 were selected out of around 60 candidates. Round 2: Technical + HR interview Generally, companies have technical and HR rounds separately. Some even have 2 technical rounds followed by an HR round(or maybe not, if you are too good). Unlike other companies, there was only one interview round for testing both the Technical and HR perspective of the candidates. 1. Introduction I introduced myself by starting with how I initialized my programming journey, then my prior work experience in startups, Play Store applications, and some other achievements. The interviewer was quite impressed by the description. Remember to brag a little! (Not too much though) It’s good to pat ourselves for our accomplishments. 2. Tell me about your work in the startups that you mentioned! Explained my part of the development that I was responsible for. 3. What technologies have you worked with so far? 4. Explain your projects mentioned in the resume. 5. Which is your favorite project? 6. Do you take users’ feedback from your applications? 7. Given a list of randomly arranged numbers, how would you find an element? Surprisingly very easy right! Actually, the interviewer was trying to get a sense of how I would build around the question. I said, “We can use linear search for this, however, if the elements were somewhat arranged, we could have done something else”. 8. Why not sort and do something? The obvious answer was time consumption. I compared the time complexities of the linear search and some of the sorting algorithms. 9. Regardless of the previous question, how would you sort them? I mentioned some sorting algorithms again and was about to explain one from it, but then the interviewer stopped me. 10.Do you know Binary Search? Can you explain the algorithm and the complexity? The results were supposed to be announced the same day itself, but it was delayed. I started feeling anxious because this might have been my last chance on-campus. I watched all the 3 parts of the Karate Kid in that single night! The next day evening the results were announced and I was more than happy to see my name on the list that I was dancing on the spot! My Advice Don’t get overwhelmed and/or inferiority complex by seeing your friends getting selected before you. You will be selected in a company that would match your skills with their requirements. Just hold on tight, keep studying and practicing. All the best! You can reach me out at: codingabby.com/contact
